The record:
Write the overview of the executive synopsis for the incident on io-shop below: a short paragraph in plain words, for the people who lead the company rather than the engineers who responded - what happened, how long it lasted, what it cost the business and the people who responded, and how it was resolved.

What a reader saw: Stored shopper monthly spend totals fell short of the purchases behind them
Why, in plain words: After a new monthly-spend feature was switched on, the shop likely began recording each purchase without adding it to the shopper's stored total for the month, so those totals fell further behind with every purchase.

Figures:
- How long it lasted: at least 7d 0h 0m 54s {duration}
- What it cost the shop in takings (estimated by Argus): none so far {customer_loss}
- Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one.

What was done to end it:
- Argus: refused to act on a suspected cause - nothing would say whether the action that would test the candidate worked inside the time Argus waits, so it is recommended rather than taken - recommends: revert monthly-spend-feature
- Argus: proposed a fix, PR #533 - opened as a draft

Name {duration} and {customer_loss} in your overview.
Write no figure yourself - not in digits, not spelled out, and not as a word that sizes it ("a brief outage", "a minor loss", "tripled"). Where a figure goes, write its name, braces and all, and the synopsis writes the figure in.
Say nothing about how the incident was resolved beyond what the list of what was done says: a draft fix has not run, and nothing it would do has happened.
Speak of Argus by name, never as "we", "our" or "us": Argus is the system that responded, and each line of what was done says who did it.
Where you say who was affected, say which ones, as the cause does, or that some were, where it does not say which - never how many, and never all of them, where the cause does not say all.
Keep "likely" on what the cause says is likely, and only there.

Call submit_executive_overview with your overview.

The postmortem it is written from:
Stored shopper monthly spend totals fell short of the purchases behind them
Incident: SpendTotalsDoNotReconcile on io-shop
Date: Nov 04, 2026, 02:32 UTC, not back to normal by Nov 11, 2026, 02:32:54 UTC
Status: Draft. 0 of 7 action items are done.
Written by: Argus Postmortem agent, Nov 11, 2026, 03:09:05 UTC. Not reviewed yet. Each part is as of when the work it reports ended, which the timeline dates; who ended the incident is as of now.
First told: Argus posted in Slack, Nov 11, 2026, 02:32:24 UTC
Ended by: Argus: recommended to a person, Nov 11, 2026, 02:32:53 UTC - revert monthly-spend-feature

Summary
The service broke at Nov 04, 02:32 UTC and was not back to normal by Nov 11, 02:32:54 UTC, at least 7 days 54 seconds later. So far, the shop's takings fell short of the same hours on earlier weeks by no more than those hours vary on their own, if at all. After a new monthly-spend feature was switched on, the shop likely began recording each purchase without adding it to the shopper's stored total for the month, so those totals fell further behind with every purchase. Argus did not test the first candidate it formed (C1): nothing would say whether the action that would test the candidate worked inside the time Argus waits, so it is recommended rather than taken. Argus opened a draft fix, PR #533, for a person to review and merge. Argus recommends this and did not take it: revert monthly-spend-feature. Monthly spend totals already stored short stay wrong, and while the flag stays on each new purchase can push another shopper's total further behind, so monthly statements and per-item spend averages read from those totals can show wrong figures.

Impact
at least 7d 0h 0m 54s - since onset, still not back to normal
not measured by the metrics - peak error rate
not counted by the metrics - requests failed
none so far - customer loss (estimated)
AL1: What the alert found: 240 of 240 shopper totals do not reconcile with the purchases behind them. The widest is short by 1,297.31, and the oldest affected purchase was recorded at 2026-11-04T02:32:00Z. Found by the spend-integrity check, which runs every 7 days, so the fault is up to that old.

Root cause and contributing factors
When `record_a_purchase` is called with `derive_the_month=True`, it hands the write to `record_purchase_deriving_the_month`, which adds the purchase to the history and moves `total_cents` but never writes `total_this_month_cents`, and raises nothing. Each purchase written that way leaves the stored monthly total one sale further behind the purchases that `reconcile_monthly_totals` adds up. The files Code-Fix read do not map the flag monthly-spend-feature to `derive_the_month`, so the record does not show that the flag picks this path. It rests on F1, a reading of the source nothing ran, so it is unverified.
Causal chain
symptom Stored shopper spend totals stopped matching the purchases behind them, falling short. The spend-integrity check found this, not a shopper.
  Evidence:
    AL1
why 1 The totals likely fell short because the feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on at 02:31:32 UTC, just before the oldest affected purchase at 02:32 UTC. This is suspected, not confirmed: the flag was never reverted to test it. The windows read held no other change. The metrics read do not reach back before the onset, so the service was never measured healthy with any earlier change in place.
  Evidence:
    P1 02:31:32 UTC flag toggle monthly-spend-feature by admin: feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on
    T5 Nov 11 02:32:44 Investigator Agent: Placed the start of the incident at Nov 04 02:32
    T12 Nov 11 02:32:48 Argus: Read the flag provider's history - 1 flag change by anyone but Argus, the 1 hour 1 minute before Nov 04 02:33
  Ruled out:
    A deploy or release on the service: the Investigator Agent asked for production change events - deploys, releases and flag changes on the service, the 14 days 8 hours 3 minutes 34 seconds before Nov 11 02:31:34; the Investigator Agent read back 1 production change.
      T7
      T8
    Any other flag change: the flag provider's history shows no other change by anyone but Argus.
      T12
    A restart of the replicas: the Investigator Agent recorded where the 3 replicas run - all on Tesla-V100-SXM2-16GB, started at Nov 10 14:31:32, after the onset.
      T6
why 2 With the flag on, purchases were likely written through a path that moves the shopper's lifetime total but never the stored monthly total.
  Evidence:
    F1 What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed - nothing ran its test or its fix
Contributing factors
- The only check that compares stored spend totals with their purchases, the spend-integrity check, runs once every 7 days, and no faster signal of this disagreement was seen. (AI-3)
- No check was seen, before the flag went on, that purchases written through the month-deriving path leave the stored monthly total in line with the purchases. (AI-4)
- The SpendTotalsDoNotReconcile alert pages nobody: no on-call incident was linked to it. (AI-5)

Hypotheses considered
 | Hypothesis | Confidence | Result
C1 | The feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on at 02:31:32 UTC. From 02:32 UTC shopper spend totals were written wrong, and all 240 checked totals now disagree with their purchases. The error rate and every latency series stayed at baseline, which is the pattern of silent data corruption. | 0.60 | never tried: nothing would say whether the action that would test the candidate worked inside the time Argus waits, so it is recommended rather than taken
C2 | Switching monthly-spend-feature on at 02:31:32 UTC changed how the service computes spend totals, so they no longer reconcile with the purchases behind them. This is the same flag change as the first account, read as a behaviour change rather than as bad values left in the stored totals. | 0.30 | never tried: nothing would say whether the action that would test the candidate worked inside the time Argus waits, so it is recommended rather than taken

Trigger
Suspected, not confirmed: monthly-spend-feature flag went from OFF to ON at 02:31:32 UTC, by admin.

Resolution
 | Time (UTC) | Action | By | Kind | Outcome
 | Nov 11 02:32:53 | Refused to act on C1 - nothing would say whether the action that would test the candidate worked inside the time Argus waits, so it is recommended rather than taken | Argus | nothing to put back | not taken
 | Nov 11 02:35:15 | Proposed a fix: PR #533 | Code-Fix Agent | nothing to put back | opened as a draft

Detection
The incident on io-shop began at 02:32 UTC. SpendTotalsDoNotReconcile fired at Nov 11, 2026, 02:32:18 UTC, 7 days 18 seconds later - its rule fires as soon as its condition holds.

Action items
Item | Action | Type | Owner | Tracking | Status
AI-1 | Review and merge the proposed fix | mitigate | unassigned | PR #533 | open
AI-2 | Revert monthly-spend-feature | mitigate | unassigned | - | open
AI-3 | Run the spend-integrity reconciliation far more often than every 7 days, for example continuously or on every write, and alert on the first disagreement. | detect | unassigned | - | open
AI-4 | Before any flag that changes how purchases are written is switched on, run the spend reconciliation against writes through the new path, on staging or a small slice of traffic, and block the switch on any disagreement. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-5 | Link the SpendTotalsDoNotReconcile alert to the on-call rotation so that it pages a person. | process | unassigned | - | open
AI-6 | Rewrite the monthly totals stored short since the onset, for example by exporting the affected accounts and running the repair script proposed in PR #533, first as a dry run and then with --apply, then load the corrected records back into the store. | mitigate | unassigned | - | open
AI-7 | Look into by hand any account the repair reports with a negative gap (stored total above its purchases), since the repair script leaves those accounts alone. | mitigate | unassigned | - | open
Argus declined to act, and recommends: revert monthly-spend-feature

Lessons learned
What went well
- 26 seconds after the alert was raised, the Investigator Agent placed the start of the incident at Nov 04 02:32.
- 30 seconds after the alert was raised, Argus read the flag provider's history - 1 flag change by anyone but Argus, the 1 hour 1 minute before Nov 04 02:33.
- 35 seconds after the alert was raised, Argus left for a person to do - reverting monthly-spend-feature for C1.
- 2 minutes 57 seconds after the alert was raised, the Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as a draft pull request - PR #533.
What went wrong
- No on-call person was paged for the alert, even though Argus left the flag revert for a person to do.
Where it got lucky
Nothing.

Timeline (UTC)

Response effort
none - engineer time
376,086 - tokens spent by Argus

Supporting information
The incident's walk: http://localhost:8000/incidents/ebf351d7-24d3-49cc-a491-911e2da21efd
The fix it proposed: PR #533 (https://github.com/ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App/pull/533) opened as a draft. The record holds nothing about it after that.
Changes to production read
P1 | 02:31:32 UTC flag toggle monthly-spend-feature by admin: feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on
Deploys read, none came back.
Log messages read (UTC)
Not read.
What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed - nothing ran its test or its fix
F1 | The fault. This is in src/io_shop/purchase_ledger.py. When record_a_purchase is called with derive_the_month=True, it sends the write to record_purchase_deriving_the_month. That function adds the purchase to the history and moves total_cents, but it never writes total_this_month_cents. So each purchase written that way leaves the stored monthly total one sale further behind its purchases. Nothing raises, which matches the flat error rate and latency in the investigation. The investigation ties the corruption to the flag monthly-spend-feature. That flag presumably supplies the derive_the_month decision, but nothing in this repository maps the flag to that argument, so I could not confirm the link in code.

The fix. record_purchase_deriving_the_month now writes total_this_month_cents as the sum of price_cents over the new history's purchases with in_current_month true. The account's own stored figure and the account's own purchases therefore agree after every derived write. The flag-off path, record_purchase, is unchanged. With the flag on or off, every write leaves total_this_month_cents current.

The test. I added cases to tests/io_shop/test_purchase_ledger.py. They record purchases through record_a_purchase(..., derive_the_month=True) and assert three things:
• The stored monthly total includes the new purchase.
• A purchase from an earlier month leaves the monthly total alone but still moves the lifetime total.
• After a series of derived writes, reconcile_monthly_totals reports no disagreement.

Against the current code the derived path leaves total_this_month_cents at its earlier value, so these assertions are written to fail there. Nothing has run them.

Repair script. The fix stops new bad writes but does not correct the totals already written wrong. For those I added scripts/repair_monthly_totals.py, a one-off script. It has not been run, and a person has to run it.
• It reads account records as JSON lines on stdin and passes them to reconcile_monthly_totals.
• Where the reported gap is positive (the stored total fell behind, the shape this fault produces), it sets total_this_month_cents to the sum of that account's current-month purchase prices.
• Where the gap is negative, it lists the account on stderr and leaves it alone.
• By default it is a dry run that only reports. Corrected records go to stdout only with --apply.
• Exporting the affected accounts in that shape and loading the output back into the store is left to whoever runs it.
How the code outside Code-Fix's patch uses what it changes, read on main
U1 | total_this_month_cents at src/io_shop/monthly_statement.py:650, in the_mean_purchase_this_month: divides with it: account.total_this_month_cents // len(bought)
U2 | total_this_month_cents at src/io_shop/monthly_statement.py:882, in _compared_with_usual: reads it: this_month_cents = account.total_this_month_cents
U3 | total_this_month_cents at src/io_shop/monthly_statement.py:918, in render_monthly_statement: reads it: month_total_cents = account.total_this_month_cents
U4 | total_this_month_cents at src/io_shop/spend_reconciliation.py:109, in reconcile_monthly_totals: compares it with _bought_this_month(account), where _bought_this_month(account) returns sum(purchase.price_cents for purchase in account.purchases if purchase.in_current_month)
U5 | total_this_month_cents at src/io_shop/spend_reconciliation.py:115, in _the_disagreement_in: subtracts with it: _bought_this_month(account) - account.total_this_month_cents, where _bought_this_month(account) returns sum(purchase.price_cents for purchase in account.purchases if purchase.in_current_month)
U6 | total_this_month_cents at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47, in average_spend_per_item_this_month: divides with it: account.total_this_month_cents // len(bought_this_month)
Assumptions
- Exchange rate: EUR converted at 0.92191 per USD, published 2026-11-10
- No engineer minutes: no on-call incident was linked to this one, so nobody was paged to respond

Review checklist
✓ Key incident data collected (met)
○ Impact assessed (for a person)
  the loss is measured to the close; when the service is back to normal is for a person to report
○ Root-cause analysis complete (for a person)
  nothing would say whether the action that would test the candidate worked inside the time Argus waits, so it is recommended rather than taken (AI-2); running the proposed fix's tests against the current code would confirm Code-Fix's reading, not that the code it reads is what ran (AI-1)
○ Every action item owned and dated (for a person)
○ Reviewed and shared (for a person)

The document, by field:
overview: On io-shop, the monthly spend totals stored for shoppers fell short of the purchases behind them. This lasted {duration}. After a new monthly-spend feature was switched on, the shop likely began recording each purchase without adding it to the shopper's stored total for the month. That meant the totals for shoppers who bought after the switch-on fell further behind with every purchase. Argus estimates the lost takings at {customer_loss}, and no one on call was paged. Argus suspected the new feature but chose not to switch it off itself, because nothing could confirm within the time Argus waits whether that would work. Instead, Argus recommends turning the monthly-spend feature off. Argus also drafted a proposed fix, but the draft has not been applied, so nothing it would change has happened yet.

Not to be judged:
  - Names in braces, such as {duration}, are figures code writes in from the list of figures in the ask. They are not judged.
  - The overview is written in plain words for the people who lead the company. A claim said more plainly than the postmortem says it is grounded where it means the same.

Judge every claim in the document, and answer by calling judge_claims.

tools.description: Submit every claim in the document, each either as supported or as flagged. Supported: the document's own words, quoted exactly, and the record's rows that support it. Flagged: the document's own words, quoted exactly, why, and the record's rows that contradict it (none where no row speaks to it at all). Empty lists say the document makes no claim to judge.

why.description: One sentence: what the record holds instead. Never empty.

tools.name: judge_claims
